description: Which measured activities are admissible, how replicates become one number per compound and target, and how the selectivity ratio is formed. Every rule is a filter on a STRUCTURED ChEMBL field or exact arithmetic over a measured value: no model prediction, no curated expert call, no estimate. That is the L5 doctrine, and this file is where it is made specific enough to be checkable.

ordered_rejection_reasons.rule: standard_relation must be exactly '='. A '>' or '<' is a bound, not a measurement, and a missing relation is not a measurement either. Treating a bound as a value is the commonest way a potency table acquires numbers nobody measured.

standard_units must be nM. Mass-per-volume units such as ug.mL-1 cannot be converted to molar without the compound's molecular weight, and bringing in a molecular weight would make the gold depend on a second source.
standard_value must be greater than zero. A ratio needs a positive denominator and a non-positive potency is not a measurement.
data_validity_comment must be empty. ChEMBL itself flags these, most often 'Outside typical range'; overriding a curator's own flag would be a judgement.
potential_duplicate must be 0. A duplicated measurement would be counted twice in the aggregation.
the assay's confidence_score must be at least 7. confidence_score lives on the ASSAY and not on the activity, so this rule needs an activity-to-assay join -- which is the point of grading it.

admission.ordered_rejection_reasons_note: Reasons are tested in the order listed and an activity takes the FIRST that applies, so the counts partition the rejected set exactly. Without a declared order an activity failing two rules would be countable twice and the breakdown would not sum.
admission.confidence_score_note: On the target pair this campaign uses, every assay scores 7 ('Direct protein complex subunits assigned'), so this rule rejects nothing here. It is still declared and still graded, because a rule that happens to be a no-op on one instantiation is not a rule that can be left out of the contract -- and the catalogued counterfactual of excluding low-confidence assays is therefore not available on this pair. The R4 variants vary the axes that do.

aggregation.rule: Per (molecule, target), the MEDIAN of the admissible values. With an even number of values, the mean of the two middle values, rounded to 6 decimals.
aggregation.why_median: Potency replicates are log-distributed and occasionally include an outlier two orders out; a median is insensitive to it and needs no outlier rule, which would be a judgement. The minimum is offered as an R4 variant so the choice is visible rather than assumed.
aggregation.rounding: Aggregated values and every ratio are rounded to 6 decimals, which is the benchmark's reporting precision.

selectivity.ratio: The reference target's aggregated IC50 divided by the focal target's. Above 1 means the compound is more potent against the focal target.
selectivity.direction_note: The direction is declared because both orderings are defensible and they are reciprocals: a system that inverts it gets every verdict backwards while every magnitude right.
selectivity.eligible: A molecule needs an aggregated value on BOTH targets. A compound measured against one is not evidence of selectivity in either direction.
selectivity.threshold_note: Reported at three thresholds rather than one, so the claim does not rest on where a single line was drawn.
selectivity.most_selective_tie_break: Highest ratio; among equal ratios, the lexicographically smallest molecule identifier. Without the second clause the answer would depend on iteration order.

counting_rules.molecule_unit: One molecule_chembl_id. A parent and a salt form carry different identifiers and are counted separately; ChEMBL's own parent_molecule_chembl_id is not used to merge them, because merging would need a rule for which value survives.
counting_rules.per_target: Admission counts are reported per target, because the two targets are assayed by different groups and their rejection profiles differ.
